label: original-phase y/a/q/c input following a/c/t/y/v/w
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase (95% of mass; never at t=0 or the delimiter, rare in copy phase), on inputs of a small token set: y (56% of mass, strongest, top activations are y after a/c e.g. "a y", "c y", "a a y"), a, q, c (and weakly t). Firing is gated by bigram context: much more likely when the previous input is a, c, t, y, v or w. Rate peaks at original positions 3-5 and drops for positions >=6. Token-only predicate has high recall (~0.9) but precision ~0.16; adding the previous-token condition gives F1 ~0.57, mass recall ~0.73. Does not fire on other letters, digits, or <DEL>. Remaining structure (exact token-pair weights, position falloff) is not captured by a simple predicate.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=4: y, a, q, c; t=3: y, a, q, c; t=5: y, a, q, c) and the previous input (most: a, c, t, y, v, w; least: p, u, g, h); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=3, L=9 & t=11, L=4 & t=2.
